title: Observe installed Claude runtime from production Windows facts
description: Objective: supply the missing production host adapter behind Claude runtime pinning. Fresh measurement at committed HEAD 6ca5da07 found `probeClaudeRuntime` and `prepareClaudeRuntimePin`, but no production `ClaudeProbePort`/`ClaudeRuntimeFactsPort`; all callers are tests or recovery inventory, while task-6cbff010 can currently succeed only by injecting `{fs,facts,clock}` from its test. Deliverable: an internal @moe/runner Windows host module that takes only bounded plain installed-runtime configuration, resolves and streams the complete native Claude closure, obtains version and platform facts through a shell-free bounded Windows process/OS boundary, feeds the production capability/observation builders, and returns immutable current facts/observation or an existing stable RUNTIME/Windows-process refusal. Unproven capabilities remain UNSUPPORTED. No caller-supplied observation, digest, version, capability answer, filesystem capability, clock, or process seam may become authority. This producer is consumed by task 6f8f1e5c (server-owned pin-request hydration; create immediately after this task) and ultimately task-6cbff010. NOT in scope: grant consumption, daemon/store orchestration, provider work launch, review, or final acceptance. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-host-runtime.ts, claude-host-runtime.js, and claude-host-runtime.test.ts. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: On Windows, the production adapter resolves a bounded local installed root/executable, streams closure digests, performs a shell-free bounded version/facts observation, and returns a production-built immutable ProviderRuntimeObservation plus ClaudeRuntimeFacts whose digest and truth class recompute.

Malformed, non-Windows, missing/reparse/escaping, unreadable, timed-out, malformed-output, and drifted observations fail closed with the exact existing RUNTIME or Windows-process reason code and refusing layer; no case upgrades UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED to PROVEN.
Only capabilities proved by the production observation are SUPPORTED; a version-only probe leaves every other capability explicitly UNSUPPORTED, with generated cases asserting a positive count.

Tests exercise the production surface and include a real Windows conformance leg (native Windows or `/init` bridge) plus mutation drills proving closure hashing, fresh version/platform facts, and fail-closed classification are load-bearing.
All three owned files are the only changed paths, each production source is below 250 physical lines, and runner/repo typecheck plus a nonzero runner test suite pass.
taskRails: Use the existing `probeClaudeRuntime`, observation builder, runtime-pin filesystem, and Windows process boundary internally; do not reimplement their authority or publish their injectable ports.
The public result may expose facts/data, never filesystem/process/clock capabilities; input is bounded plain data and error messages do not echo runtime paths, argv, environment, or secrets.
TDD every behavior; every failure test asserts exact stable reason code and layer, generated sweeps assert a positive case count, and mutation drills target the production surface.
Keep the TypeScript production file below 250 physical lines, the .js bridge one line, and commit only the three explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
PRODUCTION PART 3 — shell-free bounded version observation through the real Job boundary. Obtain the reported version by launching the validated executable with a single `--version` argument through `openWindowsProcessBoundary(request, { timeoutMs })` from platform/windows/windows-boundary.ts. That is the production Windows process seam: it is broker-mediated, job-object bounded, and structurally shell-free — do NOT reach for child_process, a shell, or `.cmd`/`.bat` indirection. Note the boundary is SYNCHRONOUS on its refusal path and returns `WindowsProcessBoundary | WindowsProcessUnknown`; a `WindowsProcessUnknown` is already a stable coded refusal at its own layer, so return it unchanged rather than re-wrapping it into a RUNTIME code and erasing which layer answered.
On the success path, read `providerStdout` with a BOUNDED accumulation (cap the bytes you retain, matching the existing `MAX_RUNTIME_TEXT_CHARS` discipline in claude-observation.ts) and await `completed`; always `close()` the boundary on every exit path including the throw path, so a failed parse cannot leak a broker process. Parse the version text conservatively — a shape you do not recognise yields a refusal, never a guessed string and never null-as-success. Pass an explicit bounded `timeoutMs`; the module's `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 30 minutes, far too long for a version probe.
Separately derive `PlatformIdentity` — `{os, arch, osVersion}` — from `node:os` inside this module, then validate it through the EXISTING `platformHostRejection` / `readHostIdentity` / `MAX_PLATFORM_IDENTITY_CHARS` helpers in platform/platform-contract.ts rather than writing your own bounds check. There is no `observeWindowsPlatform` producer in this repo (measured: linux-observation.ts and macos-observation.ts exist, no Windows sibling); reading `node:os` here is the production host boundary, and the clock is likewise constructed internally, never injected.
implementationPlan.note:

`probeVersionText` launches the validated executable through `openWindowsProcessBoundary({executable, argv: ["--version"], cwd, environment}, { timeoutMs })`. No child_process, no shell, no .cmd/.bat indirection anywhere in the production module. The environment is an allowlist of exactly SYSTEMROOT and PATH (line 59) rather than a forwarded `process.env`.

The synchronous refusal path returns the `WindowsProcessUnknown` UNCHANGED (line 143) so the Windows layer that answered stays visible instead of being restamped as a RUNTIME code — that is what lets the sweep pin `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_REFUSED` at layer `BROKER_NATIVE` rather than everything collapsing to RUNTIME.

Stdout accumulation is bounded by `MAX_RUNTIME_TEXT_CHARS` (line 148). `close()` sits in a `finally` (156-160) so it runs on every exit path including a throw — no broker outlives the observation it was opened for. Timeout is explicit: `DEFAULT_VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS` 10s, capped at `MAX_VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS` 600s, never the boundary's own 30-minute default.

Parsing is conservative: `reportedVersionOf` (165) requires both `isBoundedLabel` and `VERSION_PATTERN`, so `v24.16.0` (node's leading `v`) and empty output are refusals, never a guess and never null-as-success. Both routes are now pinned by exact message in the sweep, which is QA finding 2's fix: `...did not exit cleanly, so no version was observed` for a real nonzero exit (hostname.exe copy), `...printed output that is not the version shape this provider reports` for node.exe and for the bound-cut probe.

PlatformIdentity comes from `node:os` inside the module and is validated through the existing `readHostIdentity` helper (172), not a hand-rolled bounds check; the clock is constructed internally at 239 and never injected.

CARRIED FORWARD from `mem:gotcha-boundary-timeout-is-a-kill-bound-not-a-floor`: `timeoutMs` bounds how long the child may LIVE; `boundary.completed` resolves on the broker's completed frame. Nothing here holds the boundary open for the full bound, which is exactly why the drift race was unwinnable and is now recorded as a comment in the test file.

planningNotes.risks:
1) THE 250-LINE CAP IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND THERE IS NO FOURTH FILE. Platform gate + input hardening + two-pass inspection + boundary probe + parse + facts/observation composition is a lot for one source, and the three owned paths forbid splitting. Mitigations: compose through existing primitives rather than re-deriving, and keep EVERY fixture and helper in the .test.ts (uncapped). If it still will not fit, `moe.request_replan` — do not silently overflow and do not add an unowned file. Measure with `grep -c '' <file>`; PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts.

2) THE BOUNDARY'S DEFAULT TIMEOUT IS 30 MINUTES. `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`. A version probe that inherits it turns a hung runtime into a half-hour test hang rather than a `PROCESS_BOUNDARY_LAUNCH_TIMED_OUT` refusal. Pass an explicit bounded `timeoutMs` and cover the timeout case.

3) RESOURCE LEAK ON THE THROW PATH. The boundary spawns a real broker process. `close()` must run on every exit path including a failed version parse; otherwise a red test leaves a broker alive and poisons the rest of a `fileParallelism` run.

4) THREE LAYERS CAN REFUSE HERE — RUNTIME (claude-runtime-pin-closure), the observation builder's CLAUDE_OBSERVATION_* codes, and WINDOWS_PROCESS_* at its own layer. An assertion pinning only a code, or only 'not ok', silently detaches the moment a different layer starts answering first. Pin code AND layer everywhere, and build each fixture valid at every earlier layer so the intended guard is the one that speaks. Resist the temptation to re-wrap a `WindowsProcessUnknown` into a RUNTIME code — that erases which layer refused.

5) MEASURED FOREIGN RED, AND A WARNING SIGN INSIDE IT. `claude-launcher.windows.test.ts:178` currently gets `truthClass UNKNOWN` at `layer OUTPUT` where it expects PROVEN, on a real Windows launch on this very host. Foreign — disclose, do not repair. But note the shape: if this task's PROVEN arm also returns UNKNOWN, that is a real finding to report, NOT an invitation to weaken the assertion. A proof narrowed to accept UNKNOWN certifies nothing, and epic rail 4 keeps unverifiable evidence at UNKNOWN by design.

6) BRIDGE BYTES ARE BYTE-COMPARED by the repo's bridge guard. `export * from "./claude-host-runtime.ts";` plus a single LF — CRLF or a trailing blank line lands the file in the guard's `wrongContent` set instead of fixing `missing`.
